retriever_aggro: Not on the list. Doesn't matter.
handler_aggro: You must be what happened to Mr. Conner.
Kearney was a quiet account. You've made it loud.
Fourteen days. We were very clear about fourteen days.
handler_enrage: Fine. I'll file you under TAKEN.
Do you have any idea what a storm costs?
gus_elev_idle: Forty years of grain went through that shed.
gus_elev_greet: Told you I'd be on the porch.
gus_elev_busy: Hang on, I'm watching the floor.

start.speaker: Gus
start.text: Told you I'd be on the porch. Look at it. Kearney Co-op. Forty years of grain went up that leg and out on the trains. Now the drive shed floor is a door, and the grain goes DOWN. ...They left a yard crew. Five of 'em, walking the yard in shifts.

plan.speaker: Gus
plan.text: Clear the yard. The scale house keeps a logbook - every truck that ever drove in signed it, even theirs. Get it. Then go look at the floor in the drive shed. Don't step on the seam. Just look.

remind.speaker: Gus
remind.text: Yard crew. Logbook. Then the floor. Any order you like, as long as you're breathing at the end.

seen.speaker: Gus
seen.text: You saw the lights. ...Now you know why I don't sleep. What's the book say?

choices.text: Every truck, every pickup. And a note: DOOR CYCLES ON STORM.

seen_2.speaker: Gus
seen_2.text: On storm. Green sky, floor opens, trucks roll down. ...We need three things, then. A storm, a way to ride it down, and somebody who knows what's at the bottom. Halvorsen walked west along the river with a notebook full of storms. If anybody worked out their schedule, it's her.

after.speaker: Gus
after.text: Halvorsen went west along the river. Find her trail. I'll keep an eye on the floor.
